consequence: Software must keep bit 14 at 1; failure may lead to undefined I2C behavior.

datasheet_text: When the peripheral clock is not active, the peripheral register values may not be readable by software and the returned value is always 0x0.

consequence: Read‑modify‑write cycles may clear bits set by hardware, leading to missed events.

datasheet_text: To avoid spurious clearing of some bits, it is recommended to clear them with a load instruction where all bits which must not be altered are written with 1, and all bits to be cleared are written with ‘0 (these bits can only be cleared by software). Read‑modify‑write cycles should be avoided because between the read and the write operations another bit could be set by the hardware and the next write will clear it before the microprocessor has the time to serve the event.

consequence: Register must be accessed as half‑word (16 bits) or word (32 bits) aligned accesses only
datasheet_text: The peripheral registers have to be accessed by half-words (16 bits) or words (32 bits).

consequence: An immediate reset may be generated if T6 is cleared during a write.

The IFEM flag must be checked before each read operation to make sure that the FIFO is not empty. - After the CRYP_DIN register has been read once or several times, the FIFO must be flushed by setting the FFLUSH bit prior to processing new data.

datasheet_text: All DCMI registers have to be accessed as 32-bit words, otherwise a bus error occurs.

datasheet_text: This bit should read a logic 0 before writing to ETH_MACMIIAR and ETH_MACMIIDR.

consequence: Irregular PPS output waveforms at higher frequencies when digital rollover is used

Otherwise, with digital rollover, the PPS output has irregular waveforms at higher frequencies (though its average frequency is always correct during any one‑second window).

consequence: Time stamp update registers must be written before setting TSSTI or TSSTU bits
datasheet_text: You have to write both of these registers before setting the TSSTI or TSSTU bits in the Time stamp control register.

consequence: Incorrect sign for system‑time initialization; may cause invalid time updates.
datasheet_text: When TSSTI is set (system time initialization) this bit should be zero.

consequence: DCRST can only be written when the data cache is disabled
datasheet_text: This bit can be written only when the D cache is disabled.

consequence: ICRST can only be written when the instruction cache is disabled
datasheet_text: This bit can be written only when the I cache is disabled.

consequence: Write to lock bits is ignored or aborts if the lock key bit is set
datasheet_text: These bits are read/write but can only be written when the LCKK bit is ‘0.

datasheet_text: LOCK key write sequence: WR LCKR[16] = ‘1’ + LCKR[15:0]; WR LCKR[16] = ‘0’ + LCKR[15:0]; WR LCKR[16] = ‘1’ + LCKR[15:0]; Note: During the LOCK key write sequence, the value of LCK[15:0] must not change. Any error in the lock sequence aborts the lock.

datasheet_text: The DATATYPE bits must previously have been configured in the HASH_CR register to get a correct message representation.

consequence: Software must keep bit 14 at 1; otherwise undefined behavior.

consequence: Reading the register when the receive FIFO is empty may return 0x00000000
datasheet_text: The application must only pop the Receive Status FIFO when the Receive FIFO non-empty bit of the Core interrupt register (RXFLVL bit in OTG_FS_GINTSTS) is asserted.

consequence: After setting the force bit, software must wait at least 25 ms before the mode change takes effect.

datasheet_text: This field must not be changed until the core clears the TxFIFO Flush bit.

datasheet_text: When writing to the WWDG_CR register, always write 1 in the T6 bit to avoid generating an immediate reset.

consequence: Writing START_CONV while STOP_OP_MODE is still set may violate the required 10 µs delay and cause undefined behavior.

datasheet_text: The final signature can be read in this register once the CMDDONE information is set.

datasheet_text: A specific write sequence is used to write to the GPIOx_LCKR register. Only word access (32‑bit long) is allowed during this locking sequence.

datasheet_text: These bits can be written only when OA1EN=0.

datasheet_text: These bits can be written only when OA2EN=0.

datasheet_text: These bits can be written only when TIMOUTEN=0.

datasheet_text: These bits can be written only when TXE=1.

consequence: Read value may be stale if PVU is set
datasheet_text: Reading this register returns the prescaler value from the VDD voltage domain. This value may not be up to date/valid if a write operation to this register is ongoing. For this reason the value read from this register is valid only when the PVU bit in the IWDG_SR register is reset.

consequence: Prescaler divider cannot be changed while PVU is set
datasheet_text: PVU bit of IWDG_SR must be reset in order to be able to change the prescaler divider.

consequence: Read may return stale or invalid data if RVU bit is set.
datasheet_text: Reading this register returns the reload value from the VDD voltage domain. This value may not be up to date/valid if a write operation to this register is ongoing. For this reason the value read from this register is valid only when the RVU bit in the IWDG_SR register is reset.

consequence: Write to IWDG_RLR is ignored if RVU bit is set; reload value cannot be changed.
datasheet_text: The RVU bit in the IWDG_SR register must be reset in order to be able to change the reload value.

consequence: Write access to IWDG_WINR is protected; without the key or with WVU set, the write will be ignored or cause protection.
datasheet_text: Write access to the IWDG_PR, IWDG_RLR and IWDG_WINR registers is protected. To modify them, you must first write the code 0x0000 5555 in the IWDG_KR register. The WVU bit in the IWDG_SR register must be reset in order to be able to change the window value.

consequence: Writing values less than 0x300 is forbidden
datasheet_text: It is forbidden to write values less than 0x300 in the LPUART_BRR register.

consequence: Register can only be written when LPUART is disabled

consequence: Reading LPUART_RDR clears the RXNE flag in LPUART_ISR
datasheet_text: When FIFO mode is disabled, clearing the RXNE bit is performed by a software read to the LPUART_RDR register.

consequence: Break request may be ignored or cause transmission errors if TXE is not set.
datasheet_text: In the case the application needs to send the break character following all previously inserted data, including the ones not yet transmitted, the software should wait for the TXE flag assertion before setting the SBKRQ bit.

consequence: LPUART must not be disabled or enter low‑power mode until the transmission is complete (TC=1).
datasheet_text: After writing the last data in the LPUART_TDR register, it is mandatory to wait for TC=1 before disabling the LPUART or causing the microcontroller to enter the low power mode.

consequence: Interrupt flag is cleared when a '1' is written to the corresponding bit
datasheet_text: Write '1' to clear the interrupt

consequence: Mixed configuration of EN_CALIB_SYNTH and EN_CALIB_CBP is not recommended
datasheet_text: Both EN_CALIB_xx must be set or reset together (mixed configuration not recommended)

consequence: Software must wait 2 slow clock cycles before using the LPUART IP after setting this bit due to double resynchronization on slow clock.
datasheet_text: WARNING: the software has to wait 2 slow clock cycles before to use the LPUART IP after setting this bit due to a double resynchronization on slow clock.

consequence: Reset release is effective only after two slow‑clock periods; software must wait before using LPUART.
datasheet_text: Note: due to asynchronism slow clock/fast clock management, when the software request to release the LPUART reset by writing in the RCC_APB1RSTR.LPUARTRST, the reset release is effective only 2 slow clock periods after the APB writing. An interrupt/status flag is available to inform the software when the reset release is really done.

datasheet_text: This register is write protected. The write access procedure is described in RTC register write protection on page 421.

datasheet_text: Bits 7, 6 and 4 of this register can be written in initialization mode only (RTC_ISR/INITF = 1).

datasheet_text: The TRNG can only be accessed using 32-bit (word) accesses. References using a different size are invalid.
